source.document: Challenge Roadmap rev 2.0 (2026-10-02), status Direction approved; process approver Fitz, technical Ryan, science Harshdeep
source.transcription: FAMILIES, DOMAINS, F_SCORE and V_SCORE copied verbatim from the page's script; frequency and value labels are the owners' planning judgments, solve times are engineering estimates until Design measures them

families.name: Linear deformation and stress

est.basis: 3D bracket: remesh and direct solve with fillet refinement, one load case.

families.cust: Structural engineers designing brackets, mounts, housings and load-bearing components. Repeated geometry, material and load changes create the reuse opportunity.
families.first: One parameterized bracket family, isotropic linear elasticity, small deformation and distributed loads. Exclude plasticity, contact and fatigue. Use finite fillet radii and defined stress evaluation regions.
families.inputs: Thickness, fillet radius, hole spacing, elastic modulus, Poisson ratio, load vector and support definition. Fix geometry topology in v1.
families.preds: Displacement field or registered probes, compliance, support reactions and stress measures over defined regions.
families.ref: CalculiX or DOLFINx; compare simple beam and plate cases with analytical solutions and selected production-solver results. Refine the mesh around fillets. [S1] [S2]
families.exam: Hold out geometry combinations and load directions; test near displacement and stress limits. Check force balance, boundary conditions and positive strain energy. Prevent mesh-dependent singular peak stress from defining the target.
families.ev: Minimize mass subject to displacement and stress constraints. Use the same optimizer and budget for each model; reference-check selected designs and local perturbations.
families.build: Build geometry validity checks, a mesh-convergence harness, region-based stress extraction and a linear-superposition baseline. Benchmark against factorization reuse before funding neural search.
families.exp: Extend to additional bracket topologies, materials and thermal loading after separate evidence. Modal and buckling work can reuse meshes and assembly, but need new exams.

families.name: Transient heat conduction

est.basis: 3D plate or layered enclosure: a few hundred implicit time steps through a duty cycle.

families.cust: Thermal engineers evaluating electronics, battery enclosures and duty-cycled industrial components.
families.first: A solid plate or layered enclosure with prescribed heat histories and convection boundaries. No fluid solve, boiling, phase change or thermal runaway in v1.
families.inputs: Dimensions, conductivity, density, heat capacity, initial temperature, ambient temperature, heat-source positions and time histories, boundary heat-transfer coefficients.
families.preds: Temperature history at probes, peak temperature and its time, temperature field at registered times, and time above a specified limit.
families.ref: DOLFINx or CalculiX; analytical slab solutions and space/time refinement. Keep prescribed convection assumptions explicit. [S1] [S2]
families.exam: Hold out entire duty-cycle shapes and joint material/geometry regions. Check initial conditions, heat balance, long rollouts and off-pulse cooling. Penalize missed peaks.
families.ev: Choose thickness, material or duty cycle to meet temperature limits with minimum mass or cost. Reference-check the full time history.
families.build: Create a waveform grammar, event-aware output sampling and reduced thermal RC/POD baselines. Separate interpolation tests from longer-horizon stress tests.
families.exp: Feed validated temperature histories into thermal stress. A coupled fluid-temperature challenge needs an additional reference and interface test.

families.name: Steady heat conduction

est.basis: Fixed-topology spreader: one linear steady solve.

families.cust: Electronics and industrial thermal teams choosing heat spreaders, insulation or enclosure designs.
families.first: A fixed-topology heat spreader with one or several sources, prescribed convection and optional registered contact resistance. Conduction alone cannot predict coolant flow.
families.inputs: Plate dimensions, source size/location/power, conductivity, ambient conditions, contact resistance and prescribed convection coefficient.
families.preds: Temperature field, hotspot temperature and location, thermal resistance and boundary heat flux.
families.ref: DOLFINx or CalculiX; analytical slab and fin cases and mesh refinement. [S1] [S2]
families.exam: Hold out source arrangements and conductivity/geometry combinations. Check energy balance and applicable maximum principles; avoid claiming a universal maximum-temperature bound with internal sources.
families.ev: Choose minimum-cost material and dimensions while satisfying a hotspot limit.
families.build: Define contact boundaries, hotspot extraction and units; implement analytical/network and interpolation baselines. Measure solve cost, because many simple conduction problems are cheap.
families.exp: Add transient response and thermal stress. Keep a standalone conduction challenge even when a later challenge needs conjugate heat transfer.

families.name: Laminar internal flow

est.basis: OpenFOAM steady laminar 3D manifold, meshed and run to convergence.

families.cust: Cold-plate, microfluidic and process-component designers exploring channel geometry and pumping requirements.
families.first: Single-phase incompressible Newtonian flow through a bounded channel or manifold family. Keep each case within a justified laminar regime; no turbulence or boiling claim.
families.inputs: Channel widths and depths, branch layout parameters, inlet flow or pressure, viscosity, density and outlet boundary conditions.
families.preds: Pressure drop, branch flow distribution, velocity probes or fields, and wall shear where decision-relevant.
families.ref: OpenFOAM; Poiseuille and manifold controls and mesh convergence. Pin the distribution, solver and boundary treatment. [S3]
families.exam: Hold out aspect ratios and flow/viscosity combinations. Check continuity, nonnegative viscous dissipation and sensible pressure-flow behavior within scope.
families.ev: Minimize pumping power while meeting branch-flow requirements. Add a separate thermal objective only in a qualified coupled extension.
families.build: Build watertight geometry and mesh automation, an inlet-development policy and Reynolds-number checks. Compare resistance-network and interpolation baselines.
families.exp: Combine with solid conduction for a cold-plate challenge. Requalify interface heat transfer, fluid properties and coupled outputs.

families.name: Battery electrothermal response

est.basis: PyBaMM DFN with lumped thermal, one CC-CV charging protocol. Optimization loops and ageing runs cost far more, but v1 excludes ageing.

families.cust: Cell, pack and charging engineers selecting protocols across ambient conditions and cell parameter ranges.
families.first: One specified cell chemistry and parameter set family using a defined electrochemical/thermal model. Start from the existing battery contract after reconciliation; do not silently replace its objective or expand to pack behavior.
families.inputs: Current protocol parameters, initial state of charge, ambient/initial temperature, cooling parameters and only those cell parameters supported by the reference.
families.preds: Voltage, temperature and state histories; registered constraint margins and event times. Name the objective: CV onset, time to target SOC or another explicit event.
families.ref: PyBaMM DFN with a pinned thermal option and parameter provenance. Model agreement does not establish real-cell safety. [S4] [C1]
families.exam: Hold out protocol families and joint ambient/SOC regions. Test near voltage and temperature constraints and long rollouts. Include optimistic-boundary controls.
families.ev: Choose a feasible charging protocol under a fixed objective. Keep the fixed-optimizer EV comparison and separate false-feasible errors from feasible-design regret.
families.build: Close inherited engineering-value and public-generation gaps using current repository evidence. Resolve event interpolation, parameter uncertainty and any ageing or plating model before making claims about them.
families.exp: Extend to discharge, degradation or packs through new versions and evidence. Ageing is part of the portfolio ambition, not an automatic consequence of electrothermal accuracy.

families.name: Photonic scattering

est.basis: 3D FDTD on one GPU, run to steady port powers. 2D runs take seconds but cannot stand in for a fabricated 3D component.

families.cust: Silicon-photonics designers optimizing splitters, couplers and other compact optical components across wavelength and fabrication variation.
families.first: One parameterized passive device with fixed ports, polarization and material dispersion. Choose 2D or 3D explicitly; a reduced geometry cannot qualify a fabricated 3D component by itself.
families.inputs: Device dimensions, permitted shape parameters, wavelength, material properties and manufacturing perturbations.
families.preds: Port powers and complex scattering coefficients where required, insertion loss, reflection and bandwidth.
families.ref: Keep fdtdx as the existing pilot route; use Meep as a candidate independent cross-check. Qualify mesh, PML, run duration, port modes and phase conventions. [S5] [S6] [C1]
families.exam: Hold out geometry/wavelength combinations and fabrication perturbations. Check passivity and power balance including absorption and radiation; apply reciprocity only where assumptions justify it.
families.ev: Optimize transmission or splitting balance across a band under minimum-feature constraints. Test local perturbations of the selected design.
families.build: Repair inherited mode-phase and power-convergence issues before an authoritative exam. Build adjoint and reduced-response baselines; report geometry validity failures.
families.exp: Add fabrication-aware optimization and new port/topology families with fresh tests. Waveguide-mode evidence helps define ports but does not validate full scattering.

families.name: Eddy currents

est.basis: Harmonic GetDP solve with skin-depth meshing, from 2D or axisymmetric to coarse 3D.

families.cust: Motor, transformer and induction-component teams repeating frequency, geometry and excitation sweeps.
families.first: A conducting plate, rotor feature or lamination family under harmonic excitation in a stated magnetoquasistatic regime. Avoid blanket validity at high frequency.
families.inputs: Geometry, conductivity, permeability model, excitation frequency and amplitude, and gap dimensions.
families.preds: Loss density, total losses, impedance and the field quantities the decision needs.
families.ref: GetDP/Gmsh; analytical skin-effect cases and frequency-dependent mesh refinement. [S7]
families.exam: Hold out skin-depth/geometry ratios. Check nonnegative losses, power consistency and mesh adequacy through the conductor thickness.
families.ev: Minimize losses or mass under field and force requirements; reference-check the chosen point and neighboring frequencies.
families.build: Create a skin-depth-aware mesh policy and a complex-valued output convention. Compare reduced-order frequency-response models before broad mining.
families.exp: Couple qualified losses into a thermal model; score the resulting temperatures against a coupled reference.

families.name: Harmonic vibration

est.basis: 3D frequency sweep with resonance-adaptive points, direct solve at each frequency.

families.cust: Structural dynamics teams reducing vibration in machinery, mounts and enclosures.
families.first: Linear frequency response for one structure family with a specified damping model and excitation. Exclude nonlinear joints and impacts.
families.inputs: Geometry, stiffness, mass, damping, forcing amplitude and location, and frequency band.
families.preds: Complex response at probes, peak amplitude, resonance locations and response spectra.
families.ref: CalculiX or a qualified FE frequency-domain implementation, with analytical oscillator controls and modal-reduction comparison. [S2]
families.exam: Concentrate hidden cases near narrow resonances. Check phase conventions, damping positivity and response consistency; split by geometry rather than by individual frequency samples.
families.ev: Reduce peak response over the operating band while meeting mass and static-stiffness constraints.
families.build: Implement resonance-adaptive reference sampling, complex-error metrics and a modal-superposition baseline. A coarse frequency grid can hide the worst response.
families.exp: Add uncertainty in damping and supports. Requalify before transient or nonlinear vibration.

families.name: Magnetostatics

est.basis: 2D nonlinear motor cross-section with saturation, one rotor position. A full torque curve repeats this per position.

families.cust: Motor and actuator designers evaluating geometry, current and rotor position.
families.first: One motor cross-section or actuator family in a static or quasi-static magnetic formulation. Explicitly define saturation and permanent-magnet material models.
families.inputs: Geometry, winding/current configuration, air gap, rotor position, B–H curves and magnet properties.
families.preds: Flux linkage, field probes, stored energy, force or torque, and saturation indicators.
families.ref: Existing proposed GetDP/Gmsh route; analytical magnetic controls and refinement, with cross-checks on force/torque extraction. [S7] [C1]
families.exam: Hold out gaps, rotor positions and saturation regions. Check flux continuity and consistency of energy-derived force/torque. Do not infer full motor efficiency from static fields.
families.ev: Choose geometry and current for torque or force per mass within magnetic and geometric constraints.
families.build: Resolve the motor benchmark and material definitions; pin periodic boundaries and the force method. Add interpolation and reduced magnetic-circuit baselines.
families.exp: Extend to eddy-current losses, thermal loading and structural response through separately tested couplings.

families.name: Airfoil aerodynamics

est.basis: XFOIL viscous solve, one operating point. Higher-fidelity CFD anchors cost far more.

families.cust: Aerospace, drone and wind-energy engineers exploring section shapes and operating points.
families.first: A bounded 2D subsonic airfoil family in a declared transition and separation regime. This is not a full aircraft, rotor, bicycle-wheel or bluff-body challenge.
families.inputs: Shape coefficients, Reynolds number, Mach number, angle of attack and transition/roughness assumptions.
families.preds: Lift, drag, pitching moment, pressure distribution and reference convergence status.
families.ref: XFOIL for a scoped initial comparison; a higher-fidelity solver or experimental anchors for stronger claims. [S8]
families.exam: Hold out shape families and operating-point combinations. Distinguish nonconvergence from invalid geometry and physical failure; test sensitivity near separation boundaries.
families.ev: Improve lift-to-drag ratio across a duty envelope under thickness and lift constraints.
families.build: Measure XFOIL and interpolation cost first. Add geometric validity, transition assumptions and robust drag-error treatment; tiny absolute drag errors can change rankings.
families.exp: A 3D wing or wheel needs a new reference and scope.

families.name: Thermal stress

est.basis: Sequential thermal-to-structural 3D solve with temperature-field transfer.

families.cust: Electronics, aerospace and industrial engineers assessing expansion mismatch and heated components.
families.first: Sequential one-way coupling from a qualified temperature field into small-strain thermoelasticity. Use one topology and a defined restraint model.
families.inputs: Geometry, temperature field or history, elastic properties, thermal expansion coefficients and restraints.
families.preds: Thermal displacement, support reactions, regional stress and margin to registered limits.
families.ref: CalculiX or DOLFINx with thermal-expansion analytical controls and coupled refinement. [S1] [S2]
families.exam: Hold out material-expansion mismatch and temperature-gradient patterns. Check free-expansion and fully restrained limits; track thermal-input error propagation.
families.ev: Choose materials, clearances or dimensions to reduce thermal stress while meeting stiffness and mass requirements.
families.build: Pin the temperature-field transfer and interpolation, define the reference temperature and test constraint sensitivity. Compare sequential reference solves against surrogate composition.
families.exp: Extend to cyclic loading only with fatigue or constitutive evidence. Static thermal stress does not establish fatigue life.

families.name: Natural frequencies and modal analysis

est.basis: 3D eigensolve for the first 10–20 modes.

families.cust: Structural teams checking resonance separation during design revisions.
families.first: Small-amplitude undamped linear modes for one component family with defined supports and material density.
families.inputs: Geometry, elastic constants, density, support parameters and optional registered preload.
families.preds: First selected eigenfrequencies and mode shapes or subspaces, with mode-identification metadata.
families.ref: CalculiX or a qualified FE eigensolver; analytical beam controls and convergence checks. [S2]
families.exam: Hold out geometry/support combinations. Account for mode crossing, sign ambiguity, repeated eigenvalues and rigid-body modes; compare subspaces when needed.
families.ev: Minimize mass while keeping relevant modes outside the operating excitation band.
families.build: Build mode tracking, modal assurance/subspace metrics and a reduced-basis baseline. Do not rank raw eigenvectors without alignment.
families.exp: Reuse the qualified modal representation for harmonic response, then test damping and forced-response outputs separately.

families.name: Acoustic propagation

est.basis: Helmholtz FE solved across a frequency band with radiation boundaries.

families.cust: Acoustics engineers designing ducts, cavities and noise-control components.
families.first: Linear frequency-domain acoustics in a bounded duct or cavity family with known material and boundary impedance. Exclude nonlinear sound and turbulent source prediction.
families.inputs: Geometry, frequency, source amplitude and location, sound speed, density and boundary impedance.
families.preds: Complex pressure, transmission or insertion loss, resonant frequencies and sound-level measures with declared reference units.
families.ref: A qualified Helmholtz FE implementation in DOLFINx or GetDP; analytic duct/cavity controls, radiation-boundary and mesh checks. [S1] [S7]
families.exam: Hold out geometry/source configurations and resonance regions. Check power balance and passive-boundary behavior within the assumed model.
families.ev: Optimize attenuation over a frequency band under size or mass constraints.
families.build: Define source normalization, dB conventions and absorbing boundaries. Compare transfer-matrix and modal models, which may already be competitive.
families.exp: Extend to structural-acoustic coupling only after interface and coupled-response tests.

families.name: Optical waveguide modes

est.basis: 2D cross-section eigenmodes at one wavelength.

families.cust: Photonics teams selecting waveguide cross-sections and tolerance windows.
families.first: A registered dielectric waveguide cross-section and polarization/material family. Define which guided modes the challenge tracks.
families.inputs: Width, height, refractive indices and dispersion, cladding and wavelength.
families.preds: Effective index, mode profiles, confinement and group-index estimates where derivative quality is tested.
families.ref: MPB or another qualified eigenmode solver, with slab-waveguide controls and resolution checks. [S9]
families.exam: Hold out dimensions near cutoff and mode crossings. Resolve normalization, phase/sign and branch identity; test derivatives before claiming dispersion accuracy.
families.ev: Choose dimensions for confinement, index or dispersion targets with fabrication tolerance.
families.build: Build mode tracking and a cutoff policy; compare interpolation tables. May serve as infrastructure inside the scattering challenge rather than a challenge of its own.
families.exp: Reuse modes for scattering ports after testing consistency between the eigensolver and FDTD discretization.

families.name: Battery discharge

est.basis: PyBaMM DFN, one discharge/rest profile.

families.cust: Battery and vehicle teams evaluating load profiles and usable energy.
families.first: One cell family under discharge/rest profiles with a pinned electrochemical model. Exclude undocumented ageing and pack imbalance.
families.inputs: Current history, initial SOC and temperature, ambient conditions and registered cell parameters.
families.preds: Voltage history, delivered energy, cutoff time and specified internal states.
families.ref: PyBaMM DFN; compare SPMe/SPM and equivalent-circuit approaches as cheaper baselines. [S4]
families.exam: Hold out complete duty cycles and low-SOC/high-load combinations. Check charge accounting, event timing and voltage-limit behavior.
families.ev: Select cell size or operating profile to meet energy and power requirements without crossing model-defined limits.
families.build: Reuse battery provenance and runtime infrastructure. Establish value over reduced battery models before a standalone challenge.
families.exp: Extend to electrothermal operation and ageing only under supported parameter and validation evidence.

families.name: Electrostatics

est.basis: Linear electrostatic solve with edge refinement.

families.cust: Sensor, MEMS and insulation engineers shaping fields and capacitance.
families.first: A fixed-topology electrode/dielectric geometry with linear dielectric properties. Exclude discharge, breakdown dynamics and space charge.
families.inputs: Electrode dimensions, gaps, permittivity, applied potentials and boundary conditions.
families.preds: Potential and field, capacitance, stored energy and regional field maxima.
families.ref: GetDP or DOLFINx with capacitor analytical controls and edge-resolution studies. [S1] [S7]
families.exam: Hold out gap and permittivity ratios. Check Gauss-law consistency, boundary values and capacitance symmetry and positive energy where applicable.
families.ev: Maximize capacitance or sensitivity while constraining a registered field limit and minimum gap.
families.build: Control edge singularities through finite radii and regional measures. The solver does not predict dielectric breakdown by itself.
families.exp: Extend to electro-mechanical actuation after coupled stability and displacement tests.

families.name: Advection–diffusion

est.basis: Transient high-Péclet transport with stabilization and refinement.

families.cust: Microfluidic and process engineers evaluating mixing and transport.
families.first: A passive species in a prescribed or qualified velocity field; fixed geometry family and stated diffusion coefficients.
families.inputs: Velocity-field parameters, diffusivity, inlet/source concentrations, geometry and time horizon.
families.preds: Concentration fields, outlet uniformity, arrival time and integrated species flux.
families.ref: DOLFINx or OpenFOAM transport implementation with manufactured solutions and high-Péclet refinement. [S1] [S3]
families.exam: Hold out Péclet regimes and source patterns. Check species mass, applicable positivity and bounds, and sharp-front resolution.
families.ev: Choose geometry or operating settings to meet mixing and residence-time targets.
families.build: Separate velocity-input error from transport error. Build stabilization checks, conservative output extraction and reduced transport baselines.
families.exp: Add reactions or coupled flow through new conservation and uncertainty tests.

families.name: Porous-media flow

est.basis: Linear steady Darcy solve.

families.cust: Filter and porous-component engineers evaluating permeability, pressure drop and flow distribution.
families.first: Single-phase Darcy flow in a bounded geometry with positive-definite permeability. Add Brinkman or Forchheimer only as a new scope.
families.inputs: Geometry, permeability tensor or field parameterization, viscosity and boundary pressures or flows.
families.preds: Pressure, flux, pressure drop and regional flow uniformity.
families.ref: A qualified Darcy FE/FV implementation in DOLFINx or a selected porous-flow solver; analytic layered-media and mass-balance controls. [S1]
families.exam: Hold out anisotropy and permeability contrasts. Check mass balance and positive dissipation; preserve material field units and orientation.
families.ev: Choose material and geometry for target throughput and uniformity at minimum pumping cost.
families.build: Separate measured-permeability uncertainty from surrogate error. Compare homogenized and resistance-network models before broad search.
families.exp: Extend to thermal or reactive porous components only with measured constitutive data and new coupled tests.

families.name: Reaction–diffusion

est.basis: Stiff 1D or 2D method-of-lines integration.

families.cust: Catalyst, reactive-device and process-development teams with repeated kinetics and design studies.
families.first: One specified reaction network in a slab or simple channel family. Begin with isothermal chemistry and bounded kinetic parameters.
families.inputs: Geometry, diffusion coefficients, reaction-rate parameters, concentrations and boundary/initial conditions.
families.preds: Species concentrations, conversion, fluxes and registered reaction-front or event measures.
families.ref: A qualified DOLFINx or stiff method-of-lines implementation; analytic limiting cases and independently refined time integration. [S1]
families.exam: Hold out stiffness and diffusion/reaction ratios. Check stoichiometric conservation and nonnegative concentrations; test sharp fronts.
families.ev: Choose catalyst thickness or operating conditions to reach conversion with minimum material or residence time.
families.build: Obtain rights to kinetic data, define stiffness-aware sampling and test parameter identifiability. Reject uncalibrated kinetics as an industrial truth claim.
families.exp: Add heat release and flow only with an appropriate validation basis.

families.name: Electrical conduction

est.basis: Linear DC conduction solve with refinement around current crowding.

families.cust: Battery interconnect, busbar and power-electronics designers.
families.first: DC conduction in a fixed-topology conductor with specified conductivity and contacts. Use isothermal material properties in v1.
families.inputs: Dimensions, conductivity, terminal currents or potentials and registered contact resistance.
families.preds: Voltage, current density, equivalent resistance and Joule heating.
families.ref: DOLFINx or GetDP; resistor analytical controls and refinement around current crowding. [S1] [S7]
families.exam: Hold out contact/geometry ratios. Check charge conservation and agreement between terminal power and integrated heating.
families.ev: Minimize conductor mass while meeting voltage-drop and current-density constraints.
families.build: Define terminal and contact semantics and edge treatment. Compare resistor-network and interpolation baselines.
families.exp: Couple Joule heating to steady or transient thermal analysis; validate the coupling and temperature-dependent resistance.

families.name: Multibody dynamics

est.basis: Rigid mechanism in Chrono without contact; typically faster than real time.

families.cust: Robotics and machinery teams exploring mechanisms, trajectories and controller settings.
families.first: One rigid-link mechanism with known joints and smooth forcing. Exclude contact, impacts and changing topology in v1.
families.inputs: Link dimensions and inertias, joint parameters, initial state and actuation histories.
families.preds: Positions, velocities, joint loads, tracking error and energy over a defined horizon.
families.ref: Project Chrono with analytical pendulum and mechanism controls and time-step convergence. [S10]
families.exam: Hold out trajectories and initial states. Check kinematic constraints, energy accounting and rollout stability. Closed-loop behavior needs a separate experiment.
families.ev: Choose geometry or motion profile to minimize actuator demand under motion and load limits.
families.build: Measure existing real-time solver cost first. Define event handling and compare model reduction and analytical dynamics before surrogate training.
families.exp: Add contacts or flexible bodies only when their events and failure regimes can be resolved and tested.

families.name: Linear buckling

est.basis: Linear pre-stress solve plus geometric-stiffness eigensolve.

families.cust: Structural teams screening slender members and panels during sizing.
families.first: Elastic eigenvalue buckling of a specified component and load pattern. This estimates idealized critical load, not post-buckling capacity.
families.inputs: Geometry, elastic properties, restraints and pre-buckling load distribution.
families.preds: Critical load factors and buckling modes or subspaces.
families.ref: CalculiX or a qualified geometric-stiffness eigensolver; Euler-column and plate controls. [S2]
families.exam: Hold out slenderness and boundary configurations. Track mode switching and mesh sensitivity; reject extrapolation into invalid material regimes.
families.ev: Minimize mass while exceeding a registered buckling factor for screening.
families.build: Reuse structural geometry and mesh infrastructure. Compare classical formulas.
families.exp: Nonlinear collapse and imperfection-sensitive design need a new reference and validated evidence.

families.name: Thermal-fluid networks

est.basis: Compiled Modelica network, one operating profile; one-off compilation excluded.

families.cust: System thermal teams exploring cooling loops and operating schedules.
families.first: A fixed-topology single-phase lumped network of pipes, pumps and heat exchangers with defined component correlations.
families.inputs: Component parameters, pump and valve settings, heat loads, ambient conditions and initial states.
families.preds: Node temperatures, branch flows, pressures, energy use and transient limit violations.
families.ref: Modelica.Fluid or a qualified network solver, with a pinned simulation tool; component validation and coupled energy/mass checks. [S11]
families.exam: Hold out operating profiles and component combinations. Check mass and energy balance and event behavior under permitted flow reversals.
families.ev: Choose control settings or component sizes to meet cooling targets with minimum pump energy.
families.build: Benchmark native network solve, initialization and compilation separately. Many network models need no learned replacement.
families.exp: Consider this as the integration layer for tested component surrogates, with a system-level exam for accumulated error.

families.name: Species diffusion

est.basis: 1D or layered Fickian diffusion.

families.cust: Materials and process teams evaluating permeation, moisture ingress or release profiles.
families.first: Fickian diffusion through a slab or layered component with registered boundary conditions and no reaction or advection.
families.inputs: Geometry, diffusivity, partition coefficients where supported, initial concentration and boundary histories.
families.preds: Concentration profiles, flux, breakthrough time and integrated transfer.
families.ref: DOLFINx or a verified finite-difference solver; analytical slab solutions and time/space refinement. [S1]
families.exam: Hold out diffusivity/thickness ratios and boundary histories. Check mass balance and applicable concentration bounds.
families.ev: Choose layer thickness and material for a permeation or release target.
families.build: Test analytical and reduced-order baselines first. Distinguish fitted parameters from validated physics.
families.exp: Reuse transport infrastructure for advection or reactions.

families.name: Electrical circuits

est.basis: ngspice transient on an ordinary analog block. Large transistor-level blocks can take minutes.

families.cust: Circuit designers with repeated tolerancing, operating-corner or nonlinear block simulations.
families.first: One fixed circuit topology and licensed component-model set. Start with an analog block whose measured simulation cost warrants acceleration.
families.inputs: Component values, source waveforms, operating temperature and initial conditions.
families.preds: Voltage and current waveforms, gain and phase, settling time and specified performance metrics.
families.ref: ngspice; analytical linear-circuit controls and time-step refinement. [S12]
families.exam: Hold out operating corners and waveform types. Check Kirchhoff constraints and relevant stability and passivity properties; do not impose passivity on active circuits.
families.ev: Choose component values to meet gain, timing and power constraints across tolerances.
families.build: Confirm PDK and model rights and compare reduced macromodels. Require a cost advantage over compiled simulation.
families.exp: Complex transistor blocks may justify a higher priority than this generic ranking once measured.

families.name: Hydraulic networks

est.basis: EPANET extended-period simulation of a fixed network.

families.cust: Water and industrial network engineers evaluating flows, pressures and pump settings.
families.first: A fixed-topology pressurized water network with a defined demand and component model. Exclude water hammer in v1.
families.inputs: Pipe dimensions and roughness, node demands, pump and valve settings, and reservoir levels.
families.preds: Node pressures, branch flows, pump energy and service-limit violations.
families.ref: EPANET for water-distribution scope; analytic network controls and component calibration. [S13]
families.exam: Hold out demand patterns and control settings. Check nodal continuity and head-loss consistency. Topology changes need a declared broader scope.
families.ev: Choose pump schedules or pipe sizes to meet pressure requirements at minimum cost.
families.build: Benchmark EPANET and lookup/optimization baselines. Justify acceleration with large ensembles or online operation first.
families.exp: Add transient events, other fluids or coupled thermal behavior through a new reference contract.
